title: Difference after adjoining a disjoint set
statement: Let $J$ be a subset of a finite coordinate set, let $T$ be a subset of $J$, and let $U$ be a subset of the complement of $J$. Then the set difference between the union of $T$ and $U$ and $J$ is exactly $U$.
hypotheses_covered: $J$ is a finite subset of the coordinate set
$U$ is a subset of the complement of $J$
